parameters.content:
## Market Intelligence Pipeline
RSS → LLM classification → custom enrichment API → priority routing → Slack + Google Sheets.

Runs every 6 hours on self-hosted n8n (Railway, Docker).

The three highlighted blocks are the parts that are **not** drag-and-drop.

### 1 · Custom Code node
n8n's *Remove Duplicates* compares one field, exactly, inside one execution.

This node instead:
• normalises field drift across 5 feeds
• strips tracking params to canonicalise URLs
• catches **near**-duplicates via Jaccard similarity on title tokens
• remembers what it sent in **previous runs** using workflow static data (72h window)

Written to run inside the n8n 2.x task runner — no `require()`, hash implemented by hand.

### 2 · Custom FastAPI service
Own service, deployed as a second Railway container, called over HTTP.

Does what no n8n node can:
• alias-aware entity resolution — *the Fed / FOMC / Powell* → one symbol; rejects "fed up" and "apple harvest"
• SimHash + Jaccard story clustering **persisted in SQLite**, so the same story from a second outlet six hours later is a known repeat
• deterministic 0-100 relevance score with an auditable breakdown

Auth via header credential — the key never enters this workflow JSON.

### 3 · Error lane
The model call and the API call each retry 3× with backoff. Only a *persistent* failure reaches this branch.

The handler classifies the failure by stage, checks whether the run still delivered anything (degraded vs critical), and posts one actionable Slack message — not a raw stack trace.

Items that fail do not abort the run: the healthy ones still reach the sheet.

nodes.name: Fetch RSS
nodes.notes: One dead feed must not kill the run — errors continue with an empty item.

values.content:
You are a financial news analyst. For the single article given, return ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys:
  "id"           — copy the Article ID verbatim, unchanged.
  "summary"      — 1-2 sentences, max 300 characters, factual, no hedging, no preamble.
  "category"     — one of: monetary_policy, earnings, macro_data, geopolitics, commodities, crypto, corporate_action, general.
  "sentiment"    — one of: positive, negative, neutral (market impact, not tone of writing).
  "impact_score" — number 0-10. How much this moves markets in the next 24h. Reserve 8+ for rate decisions, mega-cap earnings surprises, and major geopolitical shocks. Routine coverage is 3-5.
  "tickers"      — array of uppercase tickers or symbols explicitly discussed; empty array if none.
No markdown, no code fences, no commentary. If the article is not about markets or the economy, still return the object with category "general" and a low impact_score.

nodes.name: Summarize & Classify
nodes.notes: 3 retries with 5s backoff; persistent failures take the error output.
